effect_estimate.comment: Headline empirical estimates reported from Round 2 parametric comparisons (Table 3), SES-adjusted OLS regressions (Table 4), billed volume/affordability analyses (Figs. 4–6), and 15-year system-level NPV cost-benefit calculations at a 12% discount rate (Table 5). Note that Table 3 means imply Rs 354 - Rs 310 = Rs 44/month difference on the total monetary cost row (computed on households non-missing on both components), whereas the text on PDF p. 6 reports Rs 69/month when summing the separate component means ((251 - 115) - (204 - 96) = 28 or sample-specific sum) and Table 4 reports the covariate-adjusted OLS difference of -Rs 32.633/month.
effect_estimate.value: Upgrading from intermittent water supply (IWS) to continuous water supply (CWS) with mandatory connection registration, metering, an increasing block tariff (Rs 48 flat + Rs 30 meter charge + Rs 10–20/kL above 8 kL), and closure of free public standpipes/borewells increased mean household ongoing monthly water expenditures from Rs 96/month (95% CI: 81.9–111.2) to Rs 204/month (95% CI: 186.6–220.3) (SES-adjusted OLS beta = +111.679 Rs/month, SE = 11.385, p < 0.01, N = 2,739), reduced amortized monthly storage/equipment investments from Rs 251/month (95% CI: 240.8–261.2) to Rs 115/month (95% CI: 109.6–120.4) (OLS beta = -133.644 Rs/month, SE = 4.875, p < 0.01, N = 3,453), reduced total monthly household monetary costs from Rs 354/month (95% CI: 334.3–374.2) to Rs 310/month (95% CI: 292.5–327.5) (OLS beta = -32.633 Rs/month, SE = 12.330, p < 0.01, N = 2,688), and reduced water-management/waiting time from 29.9 hours/month (95% CI: 28.5–31.2) to 7.4 hours/month (95% CI: 7.1–7.7), saving 22.5 hours/month on average (OLS beta = -22.632 hours/month, SE = 0.683, p < 0.01, N = 3,078). However, utility water bills rose from just over 1% of reported income (lowest wealth quintile in IWS) to just over 3% of reported income in the two lowest wealth quintiles under CWS (with no significant change in the highest quintile); billed water volume in IWS zones was 34–79% of CWS volume; free public standpipe/borewell use dropped sharply; and 15-year system-level NPV per capita fell from +Rs 2,019 (WSP demo-only cost) to -Rs 368 (WB loan with supply augmentation spread across total 3-city population) and -Rs 2,018 (allocated to demo population, yielding negative NPVs of -Rs 3,764, -Rs 3,956, and -Rs 2,753 per capita for the bottom three wealth quintiles).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF pp. 6–8, Section 4.2, Tables 3–4 & Figs. 1–6; PDF pp. 10–11, Section 5.2 & Table 5

mechanism_certainty.comment: Although the study uses a non-randomized matched-cohort design appraised with ROBINS-I, overall risk of bias is Serious (treatment was assigned in 2008 to 8 wards chosen for hydraulic isolation; household outcomes were measured only post-upgrade in 2010–2012 without household-level baseline outcomes; institutional/tariff/registration reforms were bundled with physical 24/7 pipe replacement and supply augmentation; and water bill/volume outcomes had substantial differential missingness across arms and wealth quintiles, e.g., 16% vs 68% reporting billed volumes in Quintile 1 IWS vs CWS). Per CODEBOOK.md §9, Serious ROBINS-I and bundled physical-institutional interventions cannot receive '3'; '2' applies because the authors directly observe and empirically document the administrative and tariff mechanisms (mandatory connection registration, universal metering, increasing block tariffs, and decommissioning of free public standpipes/borewells) operating on household bills, affordability, and source access.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 4, Section 2.2 & Table 2; PDF p. 5, Sections 3.1–3.2 & Footnote 4; PDF pp. 6–8, Section 4.2 & Fig. 5

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines pilot service-area rationing (8 hydraulically isolated CWS demonstration wards covering 10% of the city vs 59 IWS wards and un-piped peri-urban expansion areas: ELIGIBILITY / service_area), increasing block volumetric tariffs, fixed monthly charges, meter charges, and full cost-recovery burdens across wealth quintiles (BURDEN / fees), public protests and KUWASIP-organized public meetings that reduced initially steeper proposed CWS tariff rates (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION / participation), and risk of disconnection for non-payment alongside mandatory formal registration of unauthorized connections and utility closure of free public standpipes/borewells to curb non-revenue water (ENFORCEMENT / disconnection).

study_design.comment: Non-randomized quasi-experimental matched-cohort design evaluating the 2008 KUWASIP continuous water supply upgrade using post-upgrade panel survey rounds collected between November 2010 and February 2012, paired with document-based utility/system NPV modeling.
study_design.value: Quasi-experimental matched-cohort study using ward-level multivariate genetic matching (8 CWS intervention wards matched to 8 IWS control wards), 4-round longitudinal household panel survey over 15 months (Nov 2010–Feb 2012) with multivariable OLS econometric modeling, direct observations, and household/utility system-level cost-benefit (net present value) analysis
